pathSubtitle: Practice ordering at cafés, restaurants, and food stalls — from simple requests to handling dietary needs and complaints.

lessons.title: At a Café
lessons.situation: You walk into a small café and want to order a drink and something to eat.

dialogue.speaker: Barista
dialogue.text: Hello! What can I get you?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi. Can I have a coffee, please?

dialogue.speaker: Barista
dialogue.text: Of course. Hot or iced?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hot, please.

dialogue.speaker: Barista
dialogue.text: And anything to eat?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes. One chocolate muffin, please.

dialogue.speaker: Barista
dialogue.text: That's $5.50. Pay here or at the table?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Here, please. Thank you.

words.definition: to ask for food or drink in a café or restaurant
words.example: Are you ready to order?

words.definition: a list of food and drinks available
words.example: Can I see the menu, please?

words.definition: served cold with ice
words.example: I would like an iced coffee.

words.definition: a small sweet cake
words.example: The blueberry muffin looks delicious.

words.definition: to give money for something
words.example: I will pay by card.

lessons.title: At a Restaurant
lessons.situation: You are at a restaurant for dinner. The waiter comes to take your order.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: Good evening. Are you ready to order?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, I think so. What is the soup of the day?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: It's tomato and basil. It's very popular.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. I'll start with the soup, and then I'd like the grilled chicken for my main course.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: Excellent choice. And to drink?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: A glass of sparkling water, please.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: Of course. I'll bring your soup shortly.

words.definition: the first course of a meal
words.example: I'll have the salad as a starter.

words.definition: the biggest and most important part of a meal
words.example: For my main course, I'd like the pasta.

words.definition: cooked on a grill using direct heat
words.example: I prefer grilled fish to fried.

words.definition: water with bubbles in it
words.example: Still or sparkling water?

words.definition: in a short time, very soon
words.example: Your food will be ready shortly.

lessons.title: Dietary Requirements
lessons.situation: You have dietary restrictions and need to communicate them clearly to the waiter.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: Are you ready to order?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Almost. Before I decide, I have a question. I'm vegetarian — does the risotto contain any meat or chicken stock?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: Let me check with the kitchen. I'm pretty sure it's made with vegetable stock, but I want to confirm.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. Also, I'm allergic to nuts. Can you make sure there are no nuts in my dish?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: Absolutely. I'll flag that with the chef as well. One moment, please.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: Good news — the risotto is fully vegetarian and nut-free. Would you like that?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Perfect. Yes, I'll have the risotto, please.

words.definition: a person who does not eat meat; food with no meat
words.example: Is there a vegetarian option on the menu?

words.definition: having a bad reaction to a particular food or substance
words.example: I am allergic to shellfish.

words.definition: a liquid base made by boiling meat or vegetables, used in cooking
words.example: The soup is made with chicken stock.

words.definition: to say definitely that something is true
words.example: Let me confirm your reservation.

words.definition: to mark or draw attention to something important
words.example: I'll flag your allergy to the kitchen.

lessons.title: Sending Food Back
lessons.situation: Your food has arrived but there is a problem. You need to raise it politely but clearly.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: Here is your steak. Enjoy your meal!

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. Actually, I'm sorry to stop you — I ordered the steak medium-rare, but this appears to be well-done. Could you take it back to the kitchen?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: Oh, I'm so sorry about that. Of course. I'll have that corrected right away.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I appreciate that. Also, my side salad seems to be missing — I did order one.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.text: You're absolutely right, I apologize. I'll bring the salad immediately and make sure the steak is done correctly this time.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. No rush — I just want it right.

words.definition: a way of cooking meat — pink inside, slightly cooked outside
words.example: I'd like my steak medium-rare, please.

words.definition: meat that is cooked thoroughly with no pink inside
words.example: She always orders her steak well-done.

words.definition: a small dish served alongside the main meal
words.example: I ordered a side of fries.

words.definition: fixed or made right
words.example: The mistake was corrected quickly.

words.definition: used to say there is no hurry or urgency
words.example: No rush — take your time.

lessons.title: A Business Dinner
lessons.situation: You are hosting a client at a fine dining restaurant. The conversation blends food choices with professional small talk.

dialogue.speaker: Client
dialogue.text: This is a lovely restaurant — excellent choice.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'm glad you like it. They have a wonderful seasonal menu. Please, take your time.

dialogue.speaker: Client
dialogue.text: I'm inclined towards the lamb — what do you recommend?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The lamb here is exceptional. I'd also suggest the sea bass if you prefer something lighter. The chef sources it locally, which makes a real difference.

dialogue.speaker: Sommelier
dialogue.text: Good evening. May I suggest a wine pairing? The 2019 Bordeaux complements the lamb beautifully.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That sounds perfect. We'll go with that. And a sparkling water for the table as well, please.

dialogue.speaker: Client
dialogue.text: You clearly know this restaurant well. Do you bring clients here often?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: When the occasion calls for it, yes. I find that a good meal sets the right tone for a productive conversation.

words.definition: a menu that changes based on ingredients available in the current season
words.example: The seasonal menu features fresh autumn vegetables.

words.definition: feeling drawn to or favouring a particular option
words.example: I'm inclined towards the fish tonight.

words.definition: unusually good; outstanding
words.example: The service was absolutely exceptional.

words.definition: a trained wine expert who works in a restaurant
words.example: The sommelier recommended a full-bodied red.

words.definition: to go well with something and enhance it
words.example: A crisp white wine complements the fish perfectly.
